status_summary: Executive Order 14159 (signed 2025-01-20, published 2025-01-29 at 90 FR 8443), section 4, directs the Secretary to ensure that the primary mission of HSI is enforcement of the immigration laws and related federal laws on illegal entry and unlawful presence. News reporting of a DHS inspector general finding (article dated 2026-08-24) says HSI hours on fentanyl investigations fell about 31 percent in FY2025 while hours on immigration enforcement rose by more than 1.7 million, an increase of more than 800 percent. No DHS management directive, no transfer of non-immigration investigations to other agencies, and no ICE memo operationalizing Blackie's warrants was found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14159 was signed; its section 4 directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to ensure that HSI's primary mission is enforcing immigration laws and related federal laws on illegal entry and unlawful presence.

title: Refocus HSI on immigration offenses and operationalize Blackie's warrants
uncertainties: The inspector general report itself could not be opened: a search restricted to the DHS OIG site (oig.dhs.gov) returned a report numbered OIG-26-23 (August 2026) on HSI and fentanyl, but both the report page and its PDF returned fetch errors in two runs, so the number, title and month rest on search result titles and the hours figures rest on a news article dated 2026-08-24; the report is therefore not a timeline event or a cited source. The article says agencies were directed to provide personnel for immigration enforcement and HSI agents were reassigned, which is a shift of HSI effort but not the transfer of non-immigration work to other agencies that the Mandate describes. The law firm piece on worksite enforcement names no ICE memo, and a separate May 2025 ICE memo on home entry with administrative warrants, reported in January 2026, concerns residences and is not treated as a Blackie's warrant step. Worksite enforcement guidance since 2025-01-20 was searched only briefly. EO 14159 was reread in full on federalregister.gov (90 FR 8443 to 8448); HSI appears only in section 4 and worksite enforcement is not mentioned.
